title: Bonk Horde
pitch: Run, jump and slide through a cartoon forest while your weapons fire on their own, stack upgrades into a ridiculous build, and beat the boss before the ten-minute timer brings the final horde. Solo or with two friends.
core_loop: Pick a hero (and the host picks the map); the squad steps out of the portal.
Move to survive: run, hold jump to bunny hop, slide down slopes. Weapons attack automatically; kills drop XP gems and gold.
Level up: the game pauses and each player picks one of three upgrade offers (a new weapon, a weapon level or a tome), or banishes, skips or refreshes.
Spend gold on chests and the vendor, charge shrines for stat boosts, crack pots, take the risky shrines.
Find the boss portal and summon Old Man Timber before the 10:00 countdown ends, then kill him.
Enter the exit portal to bank the win, or stay for the final horde to push the kill score. The run ends in results and silver, then back to the menu.
win_condition: The stage boss is dead and the squad enters the exit portal: victory screen, silver banked, best time and kill score recorded.
lose_condition: Every player in the squad is down at the same time: the death screen, with silver still paid for kills made.
out_of_scope: The Desert and Graveyard maps: shown locked in map select, built as the first content update after this run ships. Desert reference study is kept in design/refs.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 multi-stage runs (portal into a second and third stage)
Procedurally generated terrain: the map layout is fixed; only interactable, portal and spawn placement is randomised per run
Quests, hero ranks, skins, challenges and the unlock shop for weapons, tomes and items: everything except one hero is unlocked from the start
Hidden bosses, secret unlock objects and character-specific secret interactions
Robux purchases, gamepasses and developer products
Global leaderboards, trading and chat features beyond Roblox defaults
Reserved-server matchmaking and cross-server parties: a server is one squad of up to three
Any use of the reference game's name, logo, character designs, item names, item art, music or jokes

systems.name: PartyService
systems.owns: the squad roster: who is in the server, each player's hero pick and ready flag, the host's map choice

systems.name: RunDirectorService
systems.owns: the run state machine (Lobby, Intro, Playing, Overtime, Victory, Wipe, Results), the stage clock, the pause flag, the difficulty value and the one simulation tick

systems.name: MapService
systems.owns: the loaded map: its heightfield, the reachable-cell grid, the anchor points, and the terrain written from it

systems.name: PlayerStateService
systems.owns: each player's run state: HP, shield, gold, downed flag, weapons, tomes, items and the resolved stat block

systems.name: XPService
systems.owns: the squad's shared XP and level

systems.name: UpgradeService
systems.owns: the offers rolled for each pending level-up choice and each player's banish, skip and refresh charges

systems.name: EnemyService
systems.owns: every enemy as plain data (position, HP, type, target, status effects), the spawn director and the snapshot stream to clients

systems.name: CombatService
systems.owns: weapon cooldown timers, projectiles, lingering zones, item procs on hit, and all damage dealt to enemies

systems.name: BossService
systems.owns: boss and miniboss entities, their attack timelines, telegraphs and thorns

systems.name: PickupService
systems.owns: XP gems, gold and powerups lying on the ground, and who collected what

systems.name: InteractableService
systems.owns: every chest, shrine, statue, vendor, pot, crate, portal and tombstone placed this run, their state, per-player use and prices, and the panels they open

systems.name: DataService
systems.owns: the persistent profile: silver, unlocked heroes, run counts and best scores

systems.name: DevService
systems.owns: Studio-only test hooks driven by the Workspace attribute BonkDev; inert in a live server

systems.name: StateController
systems.owns: the client's mirror of server state: phase, clock, squad, the local hero's state, XP, profile, and the local copy of the heightfield

systems.name: CameraController
systems.owns: the orbit camera and the mouse lock

systems.name: MovementController
systems.owns: local movement feel: slide, bunny hop, extra jumps

systems.name: EnemyRenderController
systems.owns: pooled enemy models driven by server snapshots: interpolation, limb animation, hit flash, and damage numbers

systems.name: PickupRenderController
systems.owns: gem, coin and powerup visuals and their fly-to-hero animation

systems.name: WeaponFxController
systems.owns: weapon, projectile and telegraph visuals replayed from server events

systems.name: WorldController
systems.owns: interactable models, shrine domes, and which interactable the hero can use right now

systems.name: DebugUiController
systems.owns: the plain always-wired interface: text HUD and one list panel for lobby, offers, chest, shrine, vendor, statue and results

publish.state: private place saved to Roblox by the user on 2026-10-12; not public

plan.overview: Bonk Horde. A 3D survivors-like roguelike for Roblox: third-person, auto-attacking weapons, hordes of enemies, level-up build choices, ten-minute runs. PC, gamepad and mobile. Squads of 1 to 3. Cartoon violence only, suitable for the Mild maturity label (ages 9+).
plan.pitch_and_usp: Survive a ten-minute goblin horde with a build you assemble on the fly, then beat the boss before the final horde arrives. Against the game it resembles: it is on Roblox, it is free, and it is co-op for three. Against the Roblox horde games measured in research: weapons fire themselves so the skill is movement and build choice, with jump and slide momentum on a vertical map instead of flat arenas, in a bright cartoon style.
plan.core_concept: 0 min: pick a hero, step out of the portal, one weapon, goblins trickle in, first level-up inside 30 seconds. 5 min: three or four weapons, a couple of tomes, a handful of items; you are choosing between greed (shrines, chests) and finding the boss portal while skeletons thicken. 10 min: the boss fight under a countdown, then the final horde and the question of how long you can last. 30 min: second and third runs trying a different hero and build, chasing a faster boss kill or a higher kill score. Tomorrow: silver saved toward the third hero, a best time and a best score to beat, friends to carry.
plan.player_experience: Fast, loud and a little silly. Movement should feel like the reference: quick acceleration, long downhill slides, chained hops. The power curve is the hook: one-shotting goblins at minute one, wading through two hundred enemies with five effects firing at minute eight. First win lands inside 30 seconds (first level-up with rays and confetti), a bigger one around 2 minutes (first chest reveal), and the run-defining one when the boss bar empties.
plan.audience: Roblox players who already play horde and wave survival games, mostly casual and social: friends dropping in together. Build depth and score chasing serve dedicated players. Not competitive: no PvP.
plan.market: Measured live on 2026-10-12, see design/research.md. Survive a Million Monkeys (18.8K playing, 97.6% likes) and Zombie Rush Survival (6.8K, 97.4%) prove demand for co-op horde survival; both are gun-and-wave games on flat maps with shallow builds. Robong Survivors (46 playing, 6.8M visits, 94.6% likes) is the closest survivors-like and is well liked but small; it is top-down-ish with no movement tech. Orbit Survivors is dead at 0 playing. Nobody on Roblox has the 3D momentum movement, the vertical map and the ten-minute boss-then-swarm structure together.
plan.mechanics: Movement: run, jump, hold-jump bunny hop that keeps 92% of speed, slide (speed boost on flat, acceleration downhill), extra jumps and jump height as stats. Combat: up to 4 weapons that fire on their own timers at the nearest or facing enemies; 8 weapons with distinct behaviours; 31 stats (the reference's full stats panel) fed by hero base, 12 tomes, 25 items and shrine boosts; crits and megacrits, knockback, poison, freeze, lifesteal, thorns, armour, evasion, shield that recharges out of combat. Levelling: shared squad XP from gems; on level-up the simulation pauses and every player picks from three offers rolled with rarity (Common to Legendary, shifted by Luck), with 1 banish, 5 skips and 3 refreshes per run. Economy: gold from kills and pots buys chests (price rises 30, 73, 122...) and vendor items; silver is paid at run end and persists. World: chests, charge shrines (stand in the dome for 8s, pick a boost), greed shrine (+difficulty for +gold), challenge shrine (elite pack for a free chest), vacuum shrine, statue (free item pick), vendor, pots and crates, magnet / snack / frenzy powerups, the boss portal. Timer: 10:00 countdown; at zero the final horde starts and difficulty tiers up every 30s. Co-op: instanced loot and prices per player, shared XP and gold drops, tombstone revives, enemy count and boss HP scale with squad size; solo pauses on every panel, co-op pauses only for level-ups and ghosts the chooser on other panels.
plan.progression: Short (seconds): kill, collect, level up, pick. Medium (one run): assemble 4 weapons and 4 tomes, stack items, find the portal, beat the boss, survive overtime. Long (across runs): silver toward unlocking the third hero, personal best boss-kill time and best kill score per hero shown in the menus. Deeper long-term tracks (quests, more unlocks) are out of scope for this build.
plan.content: 1 map (Mossy Woods) plus a small lobby glade. 3 heroes (Sir Clonk the knight with Sword, Zib the fox with Fire Staff, Mint the frost mage with Frost Ring; Mint costs 150 silver). 8 weapons, 12 tomes, 25 items in four rarities. 8 enemy types (Goblin Runt, Goblin Bruiser, Slime, Skeleton, Shield Skeleton, Rock Golem, Twiglet, Ghost), any of which can spawn as a crowned elite; 2 minibosses (Boulder Bro, Hamlet the Hangry); 1 stage boss (Old Man Timber). 11 interactable kinds and 5 pickups. The full roster with numbers is in game.json under roster.
plan.world: Lobby Glade: a small forest clearing with the spawn portal; purpose is the backdrop for menus and where the squad stands between runs; no enemies. Mossy Woods: the run map, about 720 x 720 studs of hills, plateaus up to 60 studs high, ramps, cliff walls at the edge, dirt paths, stone-tile ruins, towers and walls to fight around; twilight palette with blue haze, warm lanterns and drifting fireflies and embers; difficulty rises with the clock (spawn timeline in roster); unlocked from the start. The boss portal, shrines, chests and vendor are placed on randomised anchor points each run so no two runs route the same. Desert and Graveyard appear in map select as locked.
plan.story: A horde has overrun the old woods and something big is asleep under the ruins. You jump through a portal, bonk everything, wake it up on purpose and bonk that too. Told through one-line jokes on the stage card, item descriptions and the death screen; no cutscenes or dialogue.
plan.ui_ux: Screens: MainMenu, CharacterSelect, MapSelect, HUD, UpgradeOffers (with InventoryPanel and StatsPanel flanking), ChestPanel, ShrineOffers, ShopPanel, StatueOffers, BigMap, StageTitle, Banner, LevelUpFx, DownedOverlay, DeathScreen, Results, PauseMenu, TouchControls, Toast. Layout, proportions and colour roles follow design/refs/REFERENCE.md at 1920x1080 and scale down for phones; the skin is cartoon (rounded panels, thick outlines, bold rounded fonts). Common actions: start a run in 3 clicks (Play, Confirm hero, Confirm map); take an upgrade in 1 click or one key (1, 2, 3); open a chest with one key press and one click; every panel is fully usable with a gamepad (focus brackets) and by touch.
plan.tutorial: No separate tutorial level. 0:00 the stage card names the place; the quest tracker says 'Find the Boss Portal'. First 10s: only Goblin Runts, slow, so the first kills happen without input beyond moving. First level-up (about 25s) teaches the offer panel by pausing on it. A chest is always placed within 60 studs of spawn with a visible price prompt, and a charge shrine with its '!' within 120 studs. One-time hint toasts on first run: 'Hold JUMP to bunny hop', 'SLIDE downhill to go fast', 'Stand in the dome to charge the shrine'. At 5:00 a toast points at the minimap's red portal mark if the portal has not been found.
plan.art_direction: Stylised cartoon, at the user's direction (2026-10-12): the reference decides WHAT is on screen and where; the look is clean cartoon, not pixelated. Shapes: chunky and exaggerated (big heads, big hands, oversized weapons), smooth rounded forms with clean bevels. Meshes: props 100 to 2,200 triangles, enemies 500 to 1,200, heroes about 3,200, smooth shading. Textures: hand-painted cartoon at 512 to 1024 px with flat base colours, soft gradient shading and a few bold details; no visible pixels, no photo detail. Palette keeps the reference's colour roles, more saturated: grass #4C9A2E to #2F6B2A, dirt #8A5A30, stone #9AA0A6, bark #8A5230, canopy #3F8A2E with #7FC244 highlights, twilight sky #2A86B8 to #123E66, haze #2A6A8C. Lighting: cool moon key light with soft shadows, warm lantern lights, light bloom, a saturated colour grade and distance haze matched to the horizon. Skybox: painted twilight with soft puffy clouds, mountain silhouettes and a few stars. Readability: heroes get a thin cyan outline when shielded, enemies flash white on hit, elites wear a gold crown. UI: the reference's layout and colour roles (dark green panels, rarity-tinted cards, blue / green / red buttons) in a cartoon skin with rounded corners, thick dark outlines, a soft top gradient, chunky buttons with a darker lip, Luckiest Guy for titles and numbers, Fredoka One for body text, and sticker-style icons with thick outlines. A one-page style sheet (one hero, one enemy, one prop, one icon, one panel) is made first and judged against the reference before any batch work; every asset class is then compared side by side with both the reference still and the style sheet, and fidelity passes repeat until it holds.
plan.audio: Music by state: menu (laid back), forest run (upbeat adventure action), boss fight, overtime (faster), results. Ambience: night forest bed. SFX roles (63) cover interface, level-up and offers, chest and shrine interactions, each weapon's fire and impact, enemy hit / crit / death, player hurt / shield break / down / revive, movement, boss arrival / attacks / death, portal, final-horde alarm, pots and crates, vendor, timer ticks and the win and loss stings. Hit and pickup sounds are pitch-randomised and voice-limited so two hundred kills a minute stay pleasant. All audio is sourced from the Roblox Creator Store by asset id.
plan.technical_architecture: Rojo project with Knit services (server) and controllers (client), plain RemoteEvents, all tunables in Config, rules written as pure Core modules with Lune specs (Stats, Damage, XPCurve, Offers, SpawnDirector, Economy, Grid, Steering, WeaponMath, RunState, Snapshot). The horde is server-authoritative data, not instances: EnemyService simulates up to 350 enemies at 20 Hz on a spatial grid over the map's heightfield and blocked-cell grid, and streams compact buffer snapshots at 10 Hz over a RemoteEvent (6 bytes per enemy; an unreliable event would drop a full snapshot); each client renders pooled low-poly models with interpolation, procedural limb animation and distance level-of-detail, moved in one BulkMoveTo per frame. Only players use Humanoids. Weapons, hits, pickups, prices and offers are resolved on the server; clients replay visuals from events. Roblox services: Players, RunService, DataStoreService, UserInputService, ContextActionService, TweenService, SoundService, Lighting, CollectionService, AssetService (EditableImage for the minimap). Asset routes: textures, icons, portraits, the logo and the sky are generated locally with Forge (driven through its local API) and uploaded through Open Cloud or the Studio MCP's upload_image; meshes that must be exact (hero limb sets, terrain, chest, portal, weapons) are authored in Blender and uploaded through Open Cloud with the user's API key, and organic meshes (enemies, bosses, trees, statues) come from Studio's generate_mesh off an approved Forge concept; in-Studio CreateAssetAsync is not available in this Studio build (probed).
plan.data_saving: One DataStore record per player: silver, unlocked heroes, runs per hero, best boss-kill time and best kill score per map. Loaded on join with three retries; saved at run end and on leave, with a 60s autosave. If the load fails the player still plays with defaults and saving is disabled for that session so a blank profile can never overwrite a real one; a toast says progress will not be saved this session. Run state itself is never saved: a run lives and dies with its server.
plan.security: The client sends only intent: move input (through the character), interact requests, offer choices, hero and map picks. The server validates every one: offer choices must match the offers it rolled for that player; purchases check the player's gold and the server-side price; interactions check distance to the interactable; hero picks check the unlock; pickups are collected by server-side range checks, never by client claim; damage, kills, XP, gold and silver are computed only on the server. Movement is client-owned as on any Roblox character, so the server clamps speed against the player's Movement Speed stat with a tolerance and snaps back teleports. Remote calls are rate limited per player.
plan.multiplayer: A server is one squad of up to 3; friends join through Roblox's own join. The first player is host and picks the map; everyone picks a hero and readies up; the run starts when all are ready. Joining mid-run: the newcomer picks a hero and drops in beside the squad with the starter weapon and queued level-ups worth 75% of the squad's level. Leaving mid-run: their gems and gold stay shared, enemy count and boss HP rescale down on the next spawn tick, and if the host leaves the next player becomes host. If the last living player leaves, the run ends for the downed. XP is shared; gold drops credit every player; chests, shrine rewards, statue picks and vendor stock are instanced per player so nobody can take another player's loot.

monetisation.declined: No Robux in this build. The loop has to be proven fun first; out_of_scope lists it. Natural later hooks are cosmetic hero skins and extra banish or refresh charges, noted here so the code leaves room.

plan.economy: Gold (run-only): enters from kills (1 to 3 per enemy, more from elites and bosses, scaled by Gold Gain), pots, Gilded Sneakers and greed shrines; leaves through chests (rising price per chest opened, per player) and the vendor; resets every run. Silver (persistent): enters at run end from kills (1 per 100), minibosses (3 each) and the boss (10), times Silver Gain and the overtime tier multiplier; leaves only by unlocking Mint for 150. XP (run-only, shared): enters from gems dropped by every kill; consumed by level thresholds 4 + 5.5L.
plan.retention: Short runs with a strong 'one more' pull: a different hero or build each time, a best boss-kill time and kill score per hero to beat, silver accumulating toward the third hero, and friends to bring. Daily rewards, quests and seasons are out of scope for this build.
plan.social: Co-op for up to three with shared XP, revives and a results table comparing each player's kills and damage. Friends join through Roblox's join-friend flow. No trading, guilds or global leaderboards in this build.
